subject: EU prospect: clarifying default log retention & residency for prompts/outputs
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@eurobank.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Question on default log retention / residency for prompts & outputs

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the call yesterday. A quick follow-up from our security team: can you confirm Redwood's default behavior for hosted API calls originating from EU regions? Specifically:

- By default, are both the user prompt (request) and the model output (response) retained? If so, for how long?
- Does Redwood distinguish between prompts, outputs, and derivative artifacts (embeddings, logs) in the default retention window?
- If a customer requires EU-only residency and deletion on request, what is the standard process and expected completion time?

We are compiling this into our vendor review. I attached a spreadsheet with the list of states we need mapped.

Best,
Elena

Elena Rossi
Senior Information Security Manager
EuroBank S.p.A.

Attachments: eu-data-residency-matrix.csv (spreadsheet with country/regulatory notes)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@eurobank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:04:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Question on default log retention / residency for prompts & outputs

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the matrix. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Karthik (Ops) to make sure I cover policy and the operational deletion steps. High-level answers below; details and links follow.

1) Default retention (hosted API, non-enterprise-opted):
   - Request (prompt) and Response (model output) are retained by default as part of telemetry/logs. Default retention for hosted EU-region accounts is 60 days.
   - Derivative artifacts: embeddings (if you call the embeddings endpoint) are retained for 180 days by default; transient caches (KV/prefix caches) are short-lived and cleared after 7 days unless pinned by a customer.

2) Classification: we treat prompt text and model outputs as "request/response logs" for retention purposes. Other artifacts (embeddings, vector indexes) are classified separately and have their own default windows.

3) Residency: when you choose an EU region for the hosted account, all stored telemetry and logs are written to EU-only storage backends. For enterprise Dedicated/Private customers we support full on-prem/VPC deployments.

4) Deletion on request: we offer three paths:
   a) Self-service: customers with admin console access can trigger a data purge for project-level artifacts; purge jobs are scheduled immediately but have a short audit hold (see below).
   b) API-delete: an authenticated API call can request removal of request/response logs; processed within 48 hours, with background verification completed in up to 5 business days.
   c) Support-assisted: we can run an account-wide purge (used for legal/decommissioning) — typically takes 3–7 business days depending on scope and any required audit preservation.

Note on audit hold: for compliance and safety we retain a minimal tamper-evident audit record (metadata only: action timestamp, request id) for 30 days after a purge. The content itself is removed per the timelines above.

Attachments: I attached our SOC2 summary and a short residency matrix for EU regions.

I will also add a short FAQ for your vendor review.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@eurobank.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 14:18:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Question on default log retention / residency for prompts & outputs

Hi Elena — Karthik here from Ops. A few operational clarifications to complement Jonas' note:

- The 60-day default is for hosted API logs only; Dedicated customers can configure retention via the console and support SLAs for longer or shorter windows.
- When a purge is requested via the API, the delete job removes content from the primary stores first (within 48 hours). Background workers then scrub secondary caches and backups; the full pipeline completes within 5 business days. We will provide a deletion report (CSV) containing the affected request IDs once the job finishes.
- For EU residency, we do not replicate hosted EU-region customer data to non-EU regions by default; cross-region replication only happens if explicitly enabled.

If EuroBank needs a written SLT (service level) for deletion timeframes we can include a clause in the contract addendum. Happy to jump on a short call to walk your security team through the flow.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference
